title: You Can Get Google’s New Smart Glasses Next Month. I’ve Tried Them Out
snippet: Warby Parker’s and Gentle Monster’s Google and Samsung-created smart glasses have cameras like Meta’s, but these have some subtle differences when it comes to AI.
fullText:
In Gentle Monster’s hallucinatory showroom, I stared up at four robotic heads turning and talking inside floating spheres. I listened to them speak different languages. All of them were translated in my ears, on the fly, as I wore a pair of Gentle Monster smart glasses —  “Intelligent Eyewear” codeveloped by Google and Samsung that will finally arrive Dec. 10. They’ll be Google’s first pair of smart glasses since its Google Glass days more than a decade ago, and they’re landing at a time when public opinions on AI, smart glasses and data privacy couldn’t be more heated.

Google’s return to smart glasses has been promised for nearly two years, but the first waves of actual prescription-ready eyewear are only now rolling in nearly at year’s end, an unusual time for a product launch. Really, it feels more like a kickoff for efforts that will continue next year, as Google also works on AI-enabled glasses that have displays built in.

I liked these Warby Parker frames in “pine.”Scott Stein/CNET

I’d worn Google and Samsung’s smart glasses in multiple demos before, but this month for the first time I got to try on and test the final versions designed by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. I also visited two immersive showrooms the companies are opening in New York City to demo how these glasses work. These showrooms will be open by appointment.

			

More from CNET

The showrooms were like playgrounds, full of installation art to try the glasses in. Warby’s space was a series of library-themed rooms, with travel themes and whimsical sculptures. Gentle Monster’s was a stark, surreal series of rooms, blending industrial design and realistic (sometimes robotic) horses, people, chickens, floating heads, and … a big blue gentle monster.

The glasses I wore give me a strong sense of deja vu after years of reviewing Meta smart glasses and lots of others, but there are also signs of how their deeper-connected Gemini smarts could be a big difference-maker — and likely a sign of how Apple might approach its own glasses expected in 2027.

The Gentle Monster frames look good, and they also feel familiar as a smart glass wearer.Scott Stein/CNET

Clean, crisp, familiar

The various models of smart glasses across Warby Parker and Gentle Monster designs, which start at $395 and $449 respectively, all work the same: The frames do not have displays, just standard glasses lenses that support a range of prescriptions and lens types that match what Warby and Gentle Monster already offer. They have speakers on the arms that project audio, along with four beamforming microphones that filter out background noise and focus on the direction you’re facing. They have a single camera on the left side, and an LED light indicator on the right.

I got to try on all the frame designs and then wore frames with my prescription lenses popped in so that I could actually use the glasses around the exhibits. The glasses feel reminiscent of what Meta’s made for years, with similar-looking frame size and arms compared to recent Ray-Ban Gen 3 models. Most of the frames weigh around 40 grams, which felt pretty easy on my face, but I wear chunky glasses to begin with.

And the frame designs, while mostly clean and somewhat conservative, all looked really good. Warby Parker’s collection of designs came in several understated color shades (I liked the dark green Pine the best), and familiar round and square frames. 

Several good-looking frame designs by Warby Parker. Note the cameras.Scott Stein/CNET

Cameras come standard

All of the Intelligent Eyewear models across both brands have cameras, a feature that Google’s head of XR, Shahram Izadi, still sees as key to having a deep assistive experience, although he’s also open to the idea of future versions that could be camera-free like Meta’s recent Ray-Ban Audio model.

Cameras have been a big flashpoint in smart glasses over the past year, with concerns over harassment and privacy, certain countries and businesses banning them and worries about them being socially inappropriate.

These glasses use the same type of indicator system as Meta’s glasses do, flashing an LED that also auto-adjusts brightness outdoors and playing a sound when taking photos and videos.

I stared at these talking robot art heads for a long time as they spoke to me. My glasses translated.Scott Stein/CNET

Autorecognizing language translation is wild

I was particularly impressed by how Gemini can just listen to any snippet of language and translate it to what language you need, a trick that makes these glasses feel like a Swiss Army knife for travel. Several demos showed this off, including the surreal room of robotic heads that discussed Gentle Monster’s design philosophy in a handful of languages. I heard them all, sometimes with a short delay or hiccup, over 10 minutes or so.

The glasses can recognize written languages, too, in a much larger range than I’m used to: over 70. Live translation kicks in by pressing and holding two fingers on the glasses temple, and the translated voices change to try to match different speakers in a room as well as varied intonation.

Me, hypnotically staring at the heads as my glasses translated for me.Numi Prasarn/CNET

Gemini stays on 

Pressing and holding the side temple turns on Gemini, and once it’s on, it’s on until a significant pause of about 15 seconds or so. That meant that I could keep chatting and asking questions without asking “Hey Google” (or “Hey Gemini,” a new trigger phrase). I could end a session by swiping backward on the arm.

Any of the chats I have can also be turned into a note or summary instantly, hooking into Google Keep. The glasses connect with Google Maps, and Izadi promises that most of Gemini’s key features on phones will carry over to the glasses. On iPhones, the glasses will be able to triangulate across Google apps via the cloud to access Gmail, calendars and more.

Me inside an installation room, where international foods awaited my glasses analysis.Scott Stein/CNET

I found a few clever demos that showed me some promise. In a pantry installation full of world foods in Gentle Monster’s showroom, I asked Gemini to compare brands of international mayo in front of me. I could point to things and casually ask, “What is this?” And Gemini knew what I was referring to. In another demo, Gemini knew the sheet music I was holding up and played back the matching song. In another demo, I sat down and gave myself a tarot card reading — Gemini could read the cards, regardless of whether the cards were right-side up or reversed.

My tarot reading I did with the glasses on, which was saved to the connected phone.Scott Stein/CNET

Other times, Gemini said text I asked it to read was too far away, even though I could read it on a wall. Sometimes it seemed to hallucinate an odd answer to a question. (It responded with “8 minutes” to a question on a wall about whether it was OK to wait 45 minutes for a restaurant table.)

A test photo I took with the Gentle Monster glasses of me and a gentle monster.Scott Stein/CNET

Music playback, photos and videos, too

Tapping the temple arm starts and stops music, swiping changes tracks and two-finger swipes change volume (which was a bit confusing). Meanwhile, a top button on the arm takes photos and videos just like Meta glasses do, but in some demo sessions, it seemed like photos got beamed over to a Pixel phone much faster than they do to Meta’s app.

The music playback sounded good based on some quick tries in a crowded room. The audio seemed particularly loud, maybe even a bit more so than Meta’s glasses, but I’ll know more on that when I review.

How good and reliable will Google’s AI be?

The real test of Google’s Intelligent Eyewear is in how truly well connected those AI services feel and on the battery life. Meta’s up-to-eight-hour battery life on the Scriber Optics glasses I’ve been wearing the last few months tend to drain battery fast in heavy use. Will Google manage battery better, or similarly? 

It’s the AI features and Google app hook-ins that could give Google a leg up. My several hours wearing pairs and wandering through two different immersive public installation spaces only showed me hints, and really, I’m most curious about how the glasses can tap into my entire Gemini history, my Gmail, my Google Docs, or my Google Maps history. How smart and connected can they be, and how good (or unsettling) will that feel?

The Intelligent Eyewear glasses all have similar inner power buttons, LED indicators and outer camera placement, similar to Meta’s.Scott Stein/CNET

A shift in privacy

For now, it’s Google’s approach to privacy on its services for these AI glasses that has a chance to stand apart. Cameras are standard for this first wave of glasses, but Gemini treats camera feeds in AI mode differently than how photos and videos are taken otherwise, Google’s Juston Payne, senior director of project management for XR, told me. Always-on Gemini modes with camera don’t share any photos or videos for AI training or for targeting ads against, and none of the camera captures in AI modes can be seen or shared by the wearer or Google, either. Faces are autoredacted using AI on your connected phone before being sent to the cloud for AI analysis, Payne says.

That’s encouraging, but Google’s already raising questions of AI privacy with targeted ads in Gemini-powered Google search on phones and computers.

Google’s Juston Payne, wearing a Gentle Monster pair of Intelligent Eyewear outside the showroom in New York.Scott Stein/CNET

Google’s also not enabling any livestreaming from these glasses, a move that leans towards careful compared to Meta’s livestreaming modes on its glasses. “We’ll always take the conservative path right now just to rebuild trust,” Payne said. 

The glasses also won’t be able to continuously record audio ambiently to create memory summaries like Apple’s new in-beta Siri Recap feature on its recent watches can or like other smart glasses sometimes do. Also, they don’t have any environmental listening features yet, something Google says is also privacy-focused, but music recognition and other audio awareness features are on the road map. In Gemini-based audio chats with AI, Google also scrubs out voices that might be chatting near you.

But it remains to be seen how much any of this will help make anyone in public feel comfortable with someone wearing a pair of these glasses with camera-enabled AI modes on. It’s already hard to convince people that smart glasses aren’t recording people all the time, and Google’s clearly trying to restore confidence in the idea of smart glasses in public situations.

Expect more Android XR glasses next year, for sure, and, of course, more AI updates.Scott Stein/CNET

More glasses on deck

The Warby Parker and Gentle Monster models are not the only new smart wearables Google has coming: A pair of tethered mixed reality glasses that come with a processor puck and work almost like a portable VR headset, called Xreal Aura, is arriving in the next few weeks. And Google’s also starting to test its display-enabled Intelligent Eyewear ahead of a possible launch next year.

Izadi also told me that more assistive features are coming to these camera-enabled glasses, including what Google calls Guided Vision, something of an extension to the Project Astra tech Google has been working on for years. “You’ll hear more about our plans in the coming months,” Izadi said.

But agentic AI is clearly the road going forward, something both Google and Meta are expanding on for glasses. “We’ll bring more and more agentic and core AI features so that people can depend more on the AI capabilities,” Izadi said. Google’s leaning on these glasses being true phone extensions, as well as watch-connected.

But there could be a lot of cascading hardware pieces in between. Google and Samsung have already promised multiple waves of tethered and wireless smart glasses, ones with displays and ones without, and these glasses are apparently just the start.

I’m curious to see how well Warby Parker and Gentle Monster approach support for the glasses and how easy it’ll be to understand how they work. Dec. 10 isn’t far away.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Scott Stein
						

						

							Editor at Large						
					

											

								

											I started with CNET reviewing laptops in 2009. Now I explore wearable tech, VR/AR, tablets, gaming and future/emerging trends in our changing world. Other obsessions include magic, immersive theater, puzzles, board games, cooking, improv and the New York Jets. My background includes an MFA in theater which I apply to thinking about immersive experiences of the future.
															
						See full bio

In Gentle Monster’s hallucinatory showroom, I stared up at four robotic heads turning and talking inside floating spheres. I listened to them speak different languages. All of them were translated in my ears, on the fly, as I wore a pair of Gentle Monster smart glasses —  “Intelligent Eyewear” codeveloped by Google and Samsung that will finally arrive Dec. 10. They’ll be Google’s first pair of smart glasses since its Google Glass days more than a decade ago, and they’re landing at a time when public opinions on AI, smart glasses and data privacy couldn’t be more heated.

Google’s return to smart glasses has been promised for nearly two years, but the first waves of actual prescription-ready eyewear are only now rolling in nearly at year’s end, an unusual time for a product launch. Really, it feels more like a kickoff for efforts that will continue next year, as Google also works on AI-enabled glasses that have displays built in.

title: If you bought an iPhone Duo, have you kept or returned it? [Poll]
snippet: When Apple announced the iPhone Duo back in September, the company called it “the most transformational change to iPhone since the original,” and there’s no doubt that it generated a huge amount of excitement. But a new report suggests that for some buyers the novelty quickly wore off, and they ended up returning their devices. Is this just a handful of people, or is it more common … ? more…
fullText:
When Apple announced the iPhone Duo back in September, the company called it “the most transformational change to iPhone since the original,” and there’s no doubt that it generated a huge amount of excitement.

But a new report suggests that for some buyers the novelty quickly wore off, and they ended up returning their devices. Is this just a handful of people, or is it more common … ?

It’s been a very long time since any smartphone launch has generated quite so much buzz. Apple called it a breakthrough in iPhone design.

iPhone Duo features a breakthrough foldable design that’s beautiful, versatile, and durable, opening up possibilities that feel entirely new yet remarkably familiar […] 

“iPhone Duo is the most transformational change to iPhone since the original. With an entirely new design and intuitive experiences, it shows what’s possible when hardware and software are engineered together and redefines what it means to use a foldable phone,” said John Ternus.

Despite not really being the target market for the phone, I was still wowed by the launch video and remained incredibly impressed when I got some hands-on time with one.

Many couldn’t resist buying one despite the price – but The Verge notes that not everyone has ending up keeping the device. Apple allows you to return any product within 14 days for a full refund without having to give any reason. That window has come to an end for some of the first buyers and the site’s Alison Johnson spoke with some of those who’d decided to take advantage of it.

	

There were a few specific issues:

It’s too heavy and bulky

The outer screen is too small

The cameras aren’t as good as those on the iPhone 18 Pro

But the more fundamental reason for some is that it hasn’t really lived up to their hopes for a multifunctional device.

“If I can have an iPad in my pocket, that would be great.” So thought Ben Seligson, a content creator, photographer, and now former iPhone Duo owner […] “Usually I’d throw a YouTube video on the iPad or throw a podcast up. And then I start cooking dinner and leave my iPad in one spot, but I’d have my phone in my pocket if I got a text, or I needed to set a timer or something like that.” With the Duo, the phone was also the iPad on the counter, so a quick reply became much more of an interruption.

I’m curious as to whether this is just a small minority of buyers or a more common phenomenon. If you bought a Duo early enough to have hit the end of the return window, please take our poll to let us know whether you decided to keep it or return it – and do share your reasons in the comments (which are now back).

Oh, and the good news for anyone buying one now is that you’ll have a lot longer to make up your mind, with the extended return window for the holidays in place. You can now return anything bought today through January 8.

title: Google DeepMind analysis proves Signal and WhatsApp encryption is secure
snippet: The Signal protocol has long been considered the gold standard for end-to-end encrypted messaging, with Edward Snowden a notable advocate. Now a Google DeepMind analysis has “formally verified” the security of the protocol. In addition to its use in the Signal app, the same protocol is also used by WhatsApp and Google Messages, and the work has been described as “a landmark development” … more…
fullText:
The Signal protocol has long been considered the gold standard for end-to-end encrypted messaging, with Edward Snowden a notable advocate. Now a Google DeepMind analysis has “formally verified” the security of the protocol.

In addition to its use in the Signal app, the same protocol is also used by WhatsApp and Google Messages, and the work has been described as “a landmark development” … 

“Formal verification” is the term given to mathematically proving or disproving that a cryptographic algorithm or protocol satisfies its security claims under all conditions. It guarantees that there is no situation in which the protocol will fail. This is a far higher standard than traditional testing methods which seek to find vulnerabilities but cannot promise that others do not exist.

Using agentic AI to carry out formal verification is a huge breakthrough for cryptography and AI alike. It is, however, extremely computationally demanding, so Google told Wired it’s unclear as yet how practical it will be to use it more broadly.

DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process. “We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that,” Swarat Chaudhuri, a DeepMind research scientist, tells WIRED.

It’s important to note that the validation is for the protocol itself rather than the Signal app as a whole. However, encouragement can be taken from the fact that when tested against older versions of Signal that contained known vulnerabilities, it identified those and flagged them as failing formal verification.

Also worth stating is that Google was able to build on some past formal verification work already completed without the use of AI. This analysis took four weeks, and the scale of resources required has not yet been disclosed, so we shouldn’t expect a whole array of other protocols to be validated overnight. All the same, this is a very big deal.

title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
snippet: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
fullText:
Nvidia co-founder and (now former) CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

U.S. officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang, and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang, and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO

Nvidia confirmed in an SEC filing on Thursday that the board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang

November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair

Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.

November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy

Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.  

November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person” 

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”

November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation 

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”

October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy 

U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.

“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”

Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy

U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.

Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action

Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.

The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.

October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations

Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.

Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.

Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born. 

These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”

“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns, chipmaker names CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO
snippet: Nvidia gets a new chief executive, days after former CEO Jensen Huang admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
fullText:
Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as president and chief executive of Nvidia, the company said on Thursday, just a few days after he admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy, sparking a U.S. national security crisis.

In a regulatory filing, Nvidia said its board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday.

Nvidia said its current chief financial officer and executive vice president, Collete Kress, will take over as interim CEO until the company finds a permanent successor. Kress will continue to serve as the company’s CFO.

Nvidia’s shares were down nearly 12% in early morning trading on Thursday. Since Friday, the company’s stock has fallen by as much as 19%, resulting in a market cap loss of more than $855 billion.

Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it as CEO ever since. Under his leadership, Nvidia played a crucial role in developing the the graphics processing unit (GPU), a specialized chip that does graphics processing for PCs, as we know it today. The chips were not an immediate hit, and the early days of Nvidia were characterized by struggle and layoffs, but eventually, it struck on a GPU design that performed so well, it became the standard for graphics processing. 

These chips also turned out to be extremely good at doing large numbers of calculations simultaneously, which has made them popular for computation-intensive tasks like crypto mining, and more recently, training and running neural networks, which are what AI models are at their core. 

Nvidia was initially focused on making GPUs aimed at gaming, but it had already moved into general-purpose computing by 2006 with the launch of the CUDA architecture, which lets developers use the chips for other tasks, such as doing calculations and research. After AI researchers began using the company’s GPUs to train neural networks over a decade ago, Huang leaned in towards developing chips for AI and then data centers, and grew it from there into its dominant position.

Under Huang, the company has been by far the biggest benefactor of the AI industry’s skyrocketing growth, which has largely depended on Nvidia’s GPUs for training and running large language models. Before ChatGPT launched and sparked the AI boom, Nvidia shares were trading at about $15. As of last month, they had risen more than 1,450% to an all-time high of $243. It’s market cap consequently has also risen by an eye-watering $5.5 trillion since then, reaching as high as $5.88 trillion early in October. 

Revenue, of course, has also ballooned, rising more than 1,500% to $96.22 billion as of the company’s second quarter, from $5.93 billion in Q3 2023, right before the ChatGPT moment. Profits increased nearly 88 times in that period to $59.69 billion as of July 2026, from $680 million in October 2023. 

That success was predicated in large part by the AI industry’s continued development, which Huang seemingly made his personal mission. He traveled to conferences and events around the world to promote his products and AI, lobbied extensively for looser regulation after the Biden administration placed export controls on the sale of high-power AI chips to China, and cultivated a close relationship with Trump, often to Nvidia’s benefit.

The resignation and controversy come at a crucial moment for Nvidia. China was always a big market for the company, though its impact on the company’s finances has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. Chinese customers accounted for revenue of about $7.9 billion in the company’s second quarter, roughly 8% of total revenue.

Repercussions galore

The potential implications of Huang’s departure for the AI and data center industries are vast, given how active Huang, and by extension Nvidia, has been in furthering the AI boom. In particular, it raises questions about the future of Nvidia’s sprawling AI investments, which have helped bankroll everything from startups developing new technologies to the enormous data centers needed to run them. 

Under Huang, Nvidia deftly used its financial muscle to support companies buying its chips, effectively helping to finance the market for its own products, as well as lobbying Washington to relax potential rules around AI and data center regulation.

As of the end of its second quarter, Nvidia reported $99 billion worth of investments and another $25 billion of commitments. It also has $36 billion in cloud service commitments, which are arrangements that help AI cloud operators finance the GPUs and data center equipment they buy from Nvidia, with the chipmaker saying it will buy compute from them and potentially earn a share of their operators’ revenue.

Nvidia has also been investing directly in neoclouds, the companies serving a lot of the AI processing needs. In January, the company invested $2 billion in CoreWeave, and another $2 billion in Nebius in March. The chipmaker was said to be considering being a guarantor for Nscale’s planned West Virginia data center project. It’s also signed up to provide up to $105 billion worth of credit guarantees for an OpenAI data center campus in Ohio.

Nvidia’s also a major investor in the labs building the AI models that run on its GPUs, putting $30 billion into OpenAI, and $10 billion into Anthropic. It’s also backed Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab as part of a deal involving at least 1 GW of its Vera Rubin GPU systems. The chipmaker has also invested $3.5 billion in MediaTek to help the Taiwanese company develop custom AI chips that work with Nvidia’s systems.

Many investors have grown uneasy with the enormous amounts of debt companies in the space were raising to sustain the AI infrastructure buildout, and Huang’s exit throws another uncertainty-shaped wrench into the works. CoreWeave’s shares were down about 9% on Thursday, reversing part of a 25% rally on Wednesday, while Nebius is down about 16%. IREN fell 6.6%.

Nvidia’s board has also appointed Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993. As chair, Jones is likely to play a central role in Nvidia’s search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang.

Huang is the single largest personal shareholder at Nvidia, but he owns only about 3.5% of the company’s shares. Unlike many of Silicon Valley’s tech giants, he does not hold supervoting rights, and the board had the power to vote him out at any time.

Huang famously ran a very flat organization, with around 60 direct reports. There was no heir apparent or succession plan either (although two of his children also worked in executive roles at the company). Huang famously maintained tight control over the company he founded, making it challenging for Nvidia to find a path forward without him.

The industry will get its first glimpse of that next week during the quarterly conference call. Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.

“Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the company said in a statement.

Note: This story was updated to add details about Nvidia’s growth and Huang’s efforts to promote AI development, as well as its focus on China.

title: Reddit’s New AI-Powered Reviews Are Already Controversial
snippet: The platform’s test of automated product review summaries is sparking concern that advertising will replace human advice.
fullText:
Reddit announced on Tuesday that it’s testing Reviews, an AI-powered shopping feature that aggregates user comments into product summaries, commerce links, and pros-and-cons breakdowns. In a blog post, the company said it wants to organically use discussions on the platform, from conversations about skin care treatments or coffee to headphones, to help people “understand what a product is really like and feel confident deciding whether it’s right for them.”

The Reviews feature promises to make product research easier on a site that’s increasingly focused on shopping recommendations. But the announcement immediately rankled some Reddit users who are concerned it will degrade authentic human-to-human discussion and advice. Many Reddit moderators, or “mods,” tasked with keeping order of communities called subreddits, believe it’ll be hard to distinguish real opinions from straight-up advertising.

According to Reddit, the upcoming feature will surface product reviews in search results and through highlighted product mentions in comment threads, regardless of a group’s rules preventing the promotion of products by users or brands.

			

More from CNET

The test launch of Reviews, which was previewed in February and focused on electronics, will start with about 10,000 products across electronics, health and beauty, home and garden, and fashion and apparel. If the experiment works, Reddit plans to expand the feature outside the US and also increase the range of categories and products.

Mods push back

In a Reddit community for the moderators who enforce platform and subreddit rules, the new AI-powered shopping feature was greeted with skepticism and criticism. Writing in modnews, ProudnotLoud dubbed early tests “an ad-ridden, distracting mess” that made reading threads nearly impossible. 

For moderators who work to keep commercial spam out of their subreddits, the feature poses an existential threat. User nerdshark warned that communities are already being actively targeted by stealth corporate campaigns, arguing that forcing Reviews into these spaces “does vulnerable communities a huge disservice,” especially without an opt-out mechanism.

Some Reddit admins have pushed back against the backlash, clarifying that the embedded product links are search shortcuts rather than paid placements. Yet users remain unconvinced. As CouncilofStrongs countered: “From a user experience, it is an ad.”

Reddit has also recently been testing advertising in search results, which could be a way for brands to reach Reddit users who click a product name even if they aren’t paying for placement in Reddit Reviews.

Automated e-commerce

Given the amount of sites that focus heavily on human-centered reviews (you’re reading one of them), Reddit’s intent to aggregate product information through AI summaries could be seen as another way for traditional media publishers to have their content used without compensation. 

But Reddit maintains the feature is purely informational. In a statement to CNET, a Reddit spokesperson said that Reviews relies exclusively on internal platform content and “does not source, scrape or republish third-party content.” The company said that because each review links to the original discussion, users on the platform “can explore the context and go deeper. “

Reddit also said that brands can’t buy ads to get into Reddit Reviews. “What appears in Reddit Reviews is shaped by Reddit communities, not paid placement,” the spokesperson said. 

However, that reliance on organic Reddit activity brings its own vulnerabilities. One challenge Reddit may face with Reviews is trying to keep its AI focused on authentic human-written reviews versus posts that might come from marketers, coordinated astroturfing or AI-generated spam. Because the platform operates on anonymity, it’s facing an uphill battle with a massive influx of AI bots that could try to game content in Reviews.

The new feature comes alongside Reddit’s recent changes to the platform to detect spam or other manipulated content and keep bots out, including discontinuing support for RSS feeds and limiting access to its content API. The company is also restricting Old Reddit, a previous design version of the platform that has fewer ads. 

A Reddit spokesperson told CNET that the platform has “the least amount of AI slop relative to other[s]” and that it is taking “numerous steps to prevent and enforce against inauthentic content.” 

But while Reddit insists that Reviews will be centered on personal experience and uncorrupted by advertising dollars, many are worried the feature could blur the line between community research and automated e-commerce. 

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Omar Gallaga
						

						

											

								

											Omar Gallaga has covered technology, digital culture and other topics for outlets including CNET, NPR, Wired, Texas Monthly, MSNBC, Consumer Reports, The Washington Post, the Los Angeles Times, The Atlantic and the Austin American-Statesman, where he was a longtime tech reporter, editor and podcaster. He lives in the Texas Hill Country.

title: Want Apple Intelligence for Your Home Security Camera? You’ll Need These 4 Things
snippet: Apple Intelligence offers smart AI features for compatible cameras, but you’ll need to play by Apple’s rules. Here’s all the requirements.
fullText:
Aqara is one of the few camera brands that works well with Apple products.Aqara

In the past months Apple has unveiled a host of new Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features, with more on the way. And some features immediately caught my attention because they can enable security cameras on Apple devices in all-new ways. The most interesting option even adds video descriptions, essentially using AI to “read” your security clips and give you texts about what’s happening in them, so you don’t have to view them yourself.

It’s a nifty trick, one that I’ve seen come to Google Nest, Arlo, Ring, Blink and other home security camera companies in the past year or two. Now it’s Apple’s turn, but enabling this AI feature takes more work this time around. Apple wants to keep users inside its ecosystem, so there are more requirements than usual for smart video descriptions and similar capabilities. Let’s go through exactly what you’ll need.

1. A newer iPhone or iPad, updated to the latest software

The iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Duo both can run Apple Intelligence features.Patrick Holland/CNET

Apple Intelligence doesn’t run on just any device. Your first requirement is an iPhone or iPad that can handle it. If you recently downloaded iOS 27 or iPadOS 27 and received an update about Apple Intelligence now being on your device, you should be good to go.

			

More from CNET

Specifically, you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or iPhone 16 model or later to run these features. If you prefer using an iPad, you’ll need the iPad Mini (A17 Pro or later) or an iPad model with the M1 chip or later.

Before you start using security features with Apple Intelligence, make sure everything is updated – you’ll want the latest iOS if you don’t have it yet.

2. A home hub Apple device

The Mini 2 can’t compete with the large HomePod but otherwise does very well. Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Smart home devices that work with Apple Home typically need a hub to pair with, and security cameras using Apple Intelligence are no exception. That means you’ll need another Apple device that can act as a hub, and you’ve got several choices.

Apple hubs include the second-gen HomePod, the HomePod Mini and Mini 2 or an Apple TV 4K model. Apple briefly gave some iPads the ability to become home hubs but then stopped, so an iPad won’t be sufficient here.

3. A compatible security camera for Apple Home

Apple’s new camera line has 2.5K resolution and works readily with Apple devices.Ajay Kumar/CNET

You’ll need a security camera that works well with Apple Home, but that’s easier said than done. If you can wait, Apple’s own security camera line, made in partnership with LG, should be here by the end of 2026, and should have the best results.

However, those Apple cams will be very expensive, so I understand if you want to look for a more affordable option. Not many security cams currently work with Apple, but one of the best brands is Aqara, like this Aqara G3650 camera hub ($140) I’m testing right now. Aqara models go down to $40, so there’s plenty of room to save here.

Note that, at least for the base subscription, I’ve seen reports that AI features like video descriptions only work with one camera at a time, so getting a whole fleet of cams won’t make much difference here. And speaking of subscriptions, there’s one final piece you’ll want.

4. The right iCloud Plus subscription

Apple Intelligence features may require an advanced iCloud subscription.

Apple/Screenshot by CNET

You’ll want an iCloud Plus subscription to enable the full suite of Siri AI capabilities and avoid running into daily limits. But to be clear, even if you don’t use Siri AI, these security Apple Intelligence features will require at least a 2TB plan, which starts at $10 per month. That’s not surprising – video descriptions like this typically come with a subscription requirement, up to $20 per month in some cases.

Now you’ve got everything you need for Apple Intelligence security features. To get started, just go to Apple Home, go to Home Settings and make sure Apple Intelligence is toggled on. Then you should be able to choose an added camera to turn on video descriptions.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Tyler Lacoma
						

						

							Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home						
					

											

								

											Tyler has worked on, lived with and tested all types of smart home and security technology for over a dozen years, explaining the latest features, privacy tricks and top recommendations.
With degrees in business management, literature and technical writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon, gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature. title: Ring’s wheeled and flying robots will patrol your home
snippet: Some people use a whole bunch of fixed cameras to monitor their homes, but Amazon has just announced a more flexible solution through wheeled and flying robots. Both the $250 Drone Cam and $1,000 Rover Cam can respond to alarms or door and window sensor alerts in order to go check out what’s happening and send live video … more…
fullText:
Some people use a whole bunch of fixed cameras to monitor their homes, but Amazon has just announced a more flexible solution through wheeled and flying robots.

Both the $250 Drone Cam and $1,000 Rover Cam can respond to alarms or door and window sensor alerts in order to go check out what’s happening and send live video … 

Amazon says they are the first two Ring Robotics products, with more likely to follow. Both are autonomous.

Ring Drone and Ring Rover are both powered by AI Pilot, a custom-built system that uses the devices’ cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors, and cloud processing to see, think, and navigate autonomously.

AI Pilot simplifies the customer experience, starting with setup. Simply carry Ring Drone through your space or let Ring Rover autonomously explore, and it turns what it sees into a floor plan. It intelligently identifies rooms and suggests patrol points: spots worth extra attention. This could be a side door, windows, a register, or a long corridor, helping eliminate guesswork while also allowing you to add additional points customized to your space and security preferences.

When a patrol or flight is initiated, AI Pilot plans the most efficient route to get to a preset point based on the map it’s created. From there, it reacts in real time—autonomously navigating around furniture, shelving, and any obstacle it encounters.

You can set either device to patrol on a fixed schedule, as well as activate them manually, but they will also automatically respond to sensor alerts and alarms.

When a Ring camera, sensor, or alarm is triggered, [either device] automatically [moves] to previously set patrol points to investigate […] Continuous person motion detection means Ring Rover can alert you and start recording the moment it detects motion in its view—even when docked.

The Ring Rover Cam will begin shipping on December 16 for $999.99, but you can preorder it today. The Drone Cam starts shipping in late January for $249.99, but there’s no preorder yet.

title: Instagram Effect Builder lets you create images with an AI prompt
snippet: Instagram launched an Edits app for iPhone back in 2025, with a Mac version introduced just a few days ago. Meta has now supplemented this with an AI-powered Instagram Effect Builder, letting users create imagery for Stories simply by describing what they want to see … more…
fullText:
Instagram launched an Edits app for iPhone back in 2025, with a Mac version introduced just a few days ago. Meta has now supplemented this with an AI-powered Instagram Effect Builder, letting users create imagery for Stories simply by describing what they want to see … 

Instagram Edits is a free video editing app available for both iPhone and Mac. As you’d expect, the latter is the more powerful version, offering a larger workspace, more precise editing controls, and customizable keyboard shortcuts. Notably, the app supports multiple aspect ratios and allows exports as well as uploads, so can be used to produce video for any platform, not just Instagram.

Meta has now launched Instagram Effect Builder to create AI imagery for use in Instagram Stories. While it’s a standalone web-based tool, the company is describing it as an expansion of the Edits app.

One quirk is that any effect you create becomes available to any Instagram user. This usage will, however, link back to your profile.

Today, we’re expanding what you can create with Edits and introducing a new way to share your creativity on Instagram […] With Effect Builder, you don’t need design or coding skills, or prior experience making effects. Describe the look you want, preview it on your own photos, and publish. The effect shows up in Instagram Stories for anyone to use, and whenever someone uses your effect we’ll link back to your profile so that it’s easy for others to find your work.

The web app is currently limited to adult Instagram users in the US.

title: Apple has new Mac app coming to make running local AI models easy
snippet: Leaker Aaron Perris has discovered evidence of a new Mac app in the works at Apple called Harbor, which makes it easy to run local AI models across one or more Macs. more…
fullText:
Leaker Aaron Perris has discovered evidence of a new Mac app in the works at Apple called Harbor, which makes it easy to run local AI models across one or more Macs.

New ‘Harbor’ app revealed at Apple: ‘turns your Mac into a private AI inference server’

The Mac has been getting a lot more popular this year, both because of budget-friendly options like MacBook Neo but also as a tool for running AI models locally on Mac Studio, Mac mini, and more.

It seems Apple plans to lean harder into the latter use case, as leaker Aaron Perris has discovered a new Mac app called Harbor that’s been designed to turn your Mac into a private AI inference server. 

Here’s Perris’s post on X with the details:

Apple is working on a new app called Harbor

Harbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware, and nothing reaches the cloud. Connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool… pic.twitter.com/UYJBQeX4Nf

— Aaron (@aaronp613) November 10, 2026

As the post notes, here’s what the app does:

Harbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware, and nothing reaches the cloud. Connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory, enabling large models and higher concurrency that a single computer can handle alone.

And here are the feature highlights:

Setup in minutes, not hours: “Harbor automatically detects your devices over Thunderbolt 5 to form a cluster. Plug in, start, and you’re running—no manual configuration, no command line, no infrastructure expertise required.”

Download and run models directly: “Browse, download, and load open-weight models from within the app. Harbor handles model management so you can focus on the work, not the setup.”

Cluster for scale: “Connect two or more Thunderbolt 5-capable Mac computers and Harbor pools their unified memory into a single inference resource. Run models that exceed any single computer’s capacity, or serve more concurrent requests across your cluster.”

Harbor is currently in a private preview under Apple’s Claris brand, but it seems likely that we’ll see it launch to the public in the weeks and months ahead.

Are you interested in using Harbor on your Mac? Let us know in the comments.

title: Google launches Intelligent Eyewear glasses: $395+, pre-order today, ships Dec. 10
snippet: After years of development, Google is launching its second foray into smart glasses with Intelligent Eyewear that supports Android and iOS. Pre-orders start today at Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, with the audio glasses shipping on December 10. more…
fullText:
After years of development, Google is launching its second foray into smart glasses with Intelligent Eyewear that supports Android and iOS. Pre-orders start today at Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, with the audio glasses shipping on December 10.

Hands-on: Google and Samsung’s vision for Android XR glasses is 20/20

Intelligent Eyewear is meant to be worn all day rather than the sunglasses-heavy approach taken by others. The frames are 40-44 grams with the weight balanced evenly. 

There is a 12-megapixel ultra-wide camera for photos and videos (3K 30FPS or 1080p). You get image stabilization and HDR processing, while four microphones work to provide spatial audio capture. Google is also quite proud of its noise cancellation work.

	

There are two open-ear speakers for balanced audio and clear vocals. Control is done by a touchpad that accepts taps and swipes, or via voice commands, with Google debuting a new “Hey Gemini” hotword. 

Another way to control Intelligent Eyewear is through your Pixel Watch or Galaxy Watch, with Fitbit Air support coming next year:

Double pinch = “tap” gesture on touchpad to play/pause

Wrist turn = “swipe back” to close an experience

Palm-up double pinch = “tap and hold” to invoke Gemini (Pixel Watch only)

Each pair features a physical on/off switch so you can “wear them as regular glasses only.” On the privacy front, there is a white indicator light when you take a photo or video that gets saved to your gallery. If the light is covered or maliciously disabled, the glasses will stop recording, with Google running a hardware check when they are charging. Recording also stops when you take off the glasses.

Notably, Gemini commands that invoke the camera — like visual search or translation — will not save images or videos to your Gemini History. These visuals won’t be used to train AI models or for ad targeting. Additionally, the glasses will “automatically redact bystanders’ faces from these visuals before Gemini processes them.” 

Battery life (245mAh) is rated at nine hours on a single charge, with a fully topped-up charging case (Gentle Monster’s shown below) offering seven full charges. Power is transferred via contact pins located on the underside of the nose bridge. 

Android XR runs on the Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 with 2GB of RAM and 64GB of storage. Other specifications include Bluetooth 5.4, Wi-Fi 6E, and IPX4 water resistance. Samsung is responsible for engineering the hardware, while there are two eyewear brands at launch.

Warby Parker Intelligent Eyewear is available in three styles and a total of 14 variations. Alden, Reid, and Wren are inspired by the brand’s “most beloved silhouettes.” Pricing starts at $395 for optical and sun styles in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black.

The Gentle Monster Intelligent Eyewear collection features six frames in bold colors like dark red, pink, gray, and yellow, with 16 total variations. They can be paired with tinted, clear, blue, or brown lenses, with prescription options available for most designs. Pricing starts at $449 and will be available in the US and South Korea.

Intelligent Eyewear can be used for contextual visual searches, asking Gemini about your day, and having it accomplish tasks.

“…learn the story behind a street art mural you are passing by, ask for a tailored recommendation from a ‘New Arrivals’ bookshelf, or look at an event poster to check your Calendar availability on the spot.”

“…you can add items to your grocery list with a glance or check on your Uber’s status.”

“…use your glasses to catch up on your missed group chats, respond to messages, and take phone calls hands-free.”

Google Maps offers turn-by-turn directions, while there’s real-time Google Translate in over 70 languages.

Like on phones, Gemini Guided Vision “offers conversational audio descriptions to people with vision impairments.” This can be used to read fine print, identify color differences, find items, and explore unfamiliar places.

These glasses also serve as always-available headphones with support for YouTube Music, Spotify, Apple Music, and Audible. The Glasses companion app supports:

Pixel 7 and newer

Galaxy S, Galaxy S FE, Galaxy Z Fold, Flip, and Fold Ultra series running One UI 9.0 or higher

iPhone 13 Pro and up

Pre-orders for Gentle Monster and Warby Parker Intelligent Eyewear start today with retail availability on December 10.
